about: ADR-0005 rule 10 and fitness check O3: the guarded roots of SQL writes to `config`-class tables (internal/platform/store/owners/owners.gen.tsv) that do not take a step.Step. Read by tools/fitness/operation (O3, T-0391). The schema and the meaning of every field are in ADR-0005 rule 10, 'The O3 rule' (T-1221). A `system` row is permanent and is part of the ADR: adding one, or adding a table to one, is an amendment to ADR-0005. A `convert` row is a pending baseline entry: O3 prints it as pending (never a pass) and its ticket deletes it when the root takes a step.Step. Adding a caller to a `system` row is reviewed by solution-architect in the change that adds the call; it is not an amendment.

categories.signin: Sign-in, sessions, and the signing-in user's own factor enrolment (rule 10 list item 1; DM-31, DM-37 self-service)
categories.bootstrap: The first-run bootstrap (ADR-0002 platform path internal/platform/tenant/provision FirstRun and the setup-secret owner claim) and the host-local `activediq-server account init-local` command, whose authority is host access (T-0808 precedent, principal cli-account-init-local) (rule 10 list item 2)
categories.verification: Connection verification runs and what they record from the directory: run results, findings, the directory identity, the draft/verifying moves of a run, and takeover-attestation demotion signals (rule 10 list item 4, as amended by T-1221)
categories.attestation: The Entra takeover attestation callback: the IdP redirect of a sign-in that a principal started after passing the permission and step-up checks; it records only the attested_* evidence columns (rule 10 list item 9, added by T-1221)
categories.sync: Sync and inventory (rule 10 list item 4; DM-14..DM-23)

writers.reason: Activating a connection is a principal's configuration change (rule 10, connections.*). Reached today from the connections.tier0_override.acknowledge Action's Apply and from Service.Activate (lab seed). Take a step.Step; ensureEmbeddedBinding and the activation leg of Transition stay unexported helpers reached only from it.
Creating a connection is rule 10's first example (T-0093). Only the lab seed (Registry.Create, build tag lab) calls it today; the lab seed then submits the create Action or is removed.

Mixed root: Activate (principal) and the verification service (draft->verifying, verifying->draft). Split it: the moves to active run under Store.Activate's step.Step; the run's own draft/verifying moves get a narrow system writer that T-1229 adds here under category verification (pre-authorised by the T-1221 amendment; callers named). No generic Tx-taking state writer remains.

Split it: the run bookkeeping (run, findings, last_verification_id, verified_at, last_stamp_at) becomes a system writer under category verification that T-1229 adds here (pre-authorised); the credential_id swap on a passing credential_change run is a credential change (rule 10, connections and credentials) and moves to a step.Step writer called by the credential-change Action, whose plan names the passing run as its precondition.
Writes directory_identity from the V5 check of a verification run: the value is what the directory reports, not a principal's choice.
The transaction-opening wrapper of Store.SetDirectoryIdentity used by the verification service. Listed because it re-exports a system writer from the owning package (the closure rule).

Records the evidence of the Entra Global Administrator sign-in that a principal started (Attester.Start checks permission and step-up). The callback is an unauthenticated IdP redirect (ADR-0002 platform path internal/modules/connections StateTenant), so no principal and no Step exist when it runs; it writes only the attested_* columns and appends its own audit event.
Stores a demotion signal (I7(d)) observed from the directory; it can only make a takeover stale, never grant one. No product caller yet: the change that wires the signal adds its caller here.
Dead exported wrapper (no product caller) that re-exports the system writer Store.RecordDemotion from the owning package, so it breaks the closure rule. Delete it.
A tenant setting changed by a principal over HTTP (Attester.SetMaxAge checks permission and step-up inline, no Action). Becomes a connections.* Action whose Apply passes its step.Step.
Already reached only from the connections.tier0_override.acknowledge Action's Apply; pass the Action's step.Step instead of its transaction.
Reached from the connections.hybrid_link.declare Action's Apply; pass the step.Step. createLink stays an unexported helper reached from this and DiscoverHybridLink.

A link discovered by inventory sync (origin discovered) is a sync result; confirming or removing it is a principal's Action (TransitionHybridLink). No product caller yet: the ingest change that calls it adds its caller here.

Dead exported wrapper (no product caller) that re-exports the system writer Store.DiscoverHybridLink from the owning package, so it breaks the closure rule. Delete it, or list it as a system row with named callers in the ingest change that needs it.
Reached from the connections.hybrid_link.confirm and .remove Actions' Apply; pass the step.Step.
Reached from the inventory.tier0_designation.set Action's Apply; pass the step.Step.
Reached from the inventory.tier0_designation.set Action's Apply; pass the step.Step.

Registering an inventory host is an administrator's configuration change (rule 10, data sources). Service.Register has no product caller yet; it becomes the write function of an invhost Action and takes the step.Step, and the store interface method takes it too.

Creates the first owner at the setup-secret claim and the break-glass local account from the host CLI. An administrator creating an account is an authn.account.* Action (T-0096) and does not use this function.
Exported, transaction-opening, no product caller; it re-exports CreateIn. Delete it, or make it the Step-taking writer of the authn.account.create Action.
Binds the signing-in SSO account to its directory anchor during the sign-in callback (system actor).

Activates the local account once the host CLI confirms its TOTP. An administrator disabling, enabling or deleting an account is an authn.account.* Action (T-0096) with its own Step-taking writer; it does not call this function.
Sets the local account's password from the host CLI. An administrator's password reset is an authn.account.* Action with its own Step-taking writer.

Executes sqlBumpEpoch, which only increments session_epoch: it can only end sessions. Any caller that revokes sessions (role change, password or MFA reset, on demand) may call it, so its callers are not restricted.

Consumes an owner approval that names the enrolling account itself, during that account's own authority-factor enrolment (beginEnrol). Not mounted yet: the change that mounts the enrolment route adds its caller here.

A tenant owner approving another account's authority-factor enrolment (TM-D19 rule 2) is a principal's change to that account's authority, so it is an authn.account.* Action (table reclassified config by T-1221). Not mounted yet.
An owner resetting another account's authority factor is rule 10's 'reset by an administrator' (authn.account.*). Reaches the approvals write through revoke. Not mounted yet.
As Reset. Not mounted yet.
SIEM sinks are configuration Actions by rule 10 (audit retention and SIEM sinks). Called today from the CreateSiemDestination HTTP handler, audited inline, no Action.
As Store.Create (UpdateSiemDestination handler).
Idempotent seed of the built-in roles of a new tenant, in the tenant's bootstrap transaction. Built-in roles are not edited by principals.

Reached from the delegation.role.create Action's Apply and from the host CLI (grantDirectoryReader). Take the step.Step; the CLI gets a narrow bootstrap twin that T-1228 adds here under category bootstrap with callers [internal/compose/server.grantDirectoryReader] (pre-authorised by the T-1221 amendment), as GrantBootstrap already is.
Reached from the delegation.role.update Action's Apply; pass the step.Step.
Reached from the delegation.assignment.grant Action's Apply; pass the step.Step. grant stays an unexported helper reached from this and GrantBootstrap.
The host CLI's grant path that skips the grantor-holds-it check, accepted only for principal cli-account-init-local (T-0808; fitness-grantbootstrap already restricts its mentions to localaccount.go).
Reached from the delegation.assignment.revoke Action's Apply; pass the step.Step.
Grants tenant-owner to the first owner at the setup-secret claim, and to the CLI's local account only when the tenant has no owner.
Exported, transaction-opening, no product caller; it re-exports GrantIn. Delete it, or make it the Step-taking writer of the authz.* Action that adds a tenant owner.
Removing a tenant owner is a principal's authz.* change. No product caller yet; delete it or make it Step-taking.
